mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to lower S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5%, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in one month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the deteriorating labor market.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5pp, or if the correlation between UNRATE changes and 5-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as companies report lower earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances when RSAFS declines for 3 months, or if the correlation between RSAFS changes and 60-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate higher corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO increases > 2%, or if the correlation between INDPRO changes and 20-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market and strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200k, or if the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS on 20-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals strengthening demand in the housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as related industries benefit.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 45% of instances when HOUST increases for 3 months, or if the correlation between HOUST changes and 60-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4%, it signals inflationary pressure and potential monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS > 4%, or if the joint effect of CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS on 5-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a high level of real GDP (GDPC1) relative to its 12-month moving average suggests strong economic fundamentals, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 45% of instances when GDPC1 is above its 12-month moving average, or if the correlation between GDPC1 relative strength and 60-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).
